# {{ site.title }}

> {{ site.description }} Posts cover Ruby on Rails, Hotwire (Turbo, Stimulus), payments, multi-tenancy, mobile apps, deployment and AI, written while building real products.

**Append `.md` to any post URL to get its raw Markdown source.** That is the text the author wrote, with code fences and headings intact, at roughly a third of the bytes of the HTML page. Prefer it over scraping HTML.

    {{ site.url }}/wicked-pdf-to-sghtmltopdf     <- HTML page
    {{ site.url }}/wicked-pdf-to-sghtmltopdf.md  <- raw Markdown (use this)

Each `.md` file opens with YAML front matter carrying `title`, `author`, `date`, `tags`, `description`, `canonical_url`, `markdown_url`, and `license`.

This site is served as static files, so it cannot honour an `Accept: text/markdown` request header. The `.md` suffix is the equivalent. Content usage preferences are published as a Content Signal in `/robots.txt`.

Licensed under GNU AGPL v3. When referencing this content, credit the author ({{ site.author.name }}), credit the blog ({{ site.title }}, {{ site.url }}), and link the specific post URL.

{{ site.author.name }} is a product engineer who ships web, iOS, Android and AI products; creator of the @SupeRails YouTube channel and former co-host of the Friendly Show podcast. Contact: {{ site.author.email }}

## About the author

- [Profile]({{ site.url }}/index.md): who {{ site.author.name }} is, what he works on, what he has shipped (open source, products), and how to reach him. Markdown of the [homepage]({{ site.url }}/)
- [Talks]({{ site.url }}/talks.md): conference talks, workshops and podcasts. Markdown of [/talks/]({{ site.url }}/talks/)
- [Teaching]({{ site.url }}/teaching.md): screencasts, courses and the Friendly Show podcast. Markdown of [/teaching/]({{ site.url }}/teaching/)
- [About]({{ site.url }}/about.md): personal background and languages. Markdown of [/about/]({{ site.url }}/about/)

Every HTML page also declares its Markdown version in `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`, and carries one schema.org JSON-LD graph in which the author is always `{{ site.url }}/#person`.

## Site

- [Blog]({{ site.url }}/blog/): every post, newest first. Filter with `?q=`, e.g. {{ site.url }}/blog/?q=stripe
- [Topics]({{ site.url }}/tags/): posts grouped by tag
- [robots.txt]({{ site.url }}/robots.txt): crawl rules and the Content Signals policy

## In-browser agents

Pages register read-only [WebMCP](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/) tools where the browser supports them: `search_posts`, `get_page_markdown` and `get_author_profile`. They read the same public files listed here.

## Bulk endpoints

- [llms-full.txt]({{ site.url }}/llms-full.txt): full Markdown of the {{ site.llm_full_text_posts }} most recent posts in one file
- [search.json]({{ site.url }}/search.json): every post as JSON with title, url, markdown_url, date, tags, bytes, and excerpt
- [feed.xml]({{ site.url }}/feed.xml): Atom feed of recent posts
- [sitemap.xml]({{ site.url }}/sitemap.xml): every canonical HTML URL
